paper_metadata.title: QUASI-BINARY ENCODING BASED QUANTUM ALTERNATING OPERATOR ANSATZ

summary: This paper proposes a quasi-binary-encoding QAOA for portfolio optimization, using 18 qubits for the main six-stock instance and 12 qubits for a two-asset mixability study. Reported approximation ratios range from 0.791 to 0.905 for Normal-QAOA and from 0.907 to 0.994 for CVaR-QAOA across repeated runs, with the best reported tail performance achieved by IQAOA under CVaR-QAOA; the precision-increasing iterative method reuses 18 qubits over six iterations and improves solution quality further.

experiments.description: Quasi-binary encoding based QAOA (QB-QAOA) applied to portfolio optimization with numerical simulations on six NASDAQ stocks and a two-asset mixability study, including Normal-QAOA and CVaR-QAOA variants with multiple parameter-scheduling methods.

algorithm.variant: Quasi-binary encoding based QAOA (QB-QAOA); Normal-QAOA and CVaR-QAOA variants; hard-constraint QAOA/QAOAz
algorithm.convergence_criteria: 1000 COBYLA iterations per parameter set; 20 random initial parameter sets for Sample20

hyperparameters.iqaoa_method: use (p-1)-layer optimum as initial values, last gamma/beta set to 0

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Sample20 uses random uniform initial parameters in the stated ranges; OLS uses two optimized schedule parameters; IOLS and IQAOA initialize from lower-depth optimal parameters; initial state prepared from a greedy feasible solution encoded with X gates

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Quasi-binary encoding of integer variables y_i in [0,R_i]; each variable uses at most 2 log2(R_i+1) qubits, with bits grouped by powers of two; feasible states preserved by a custom mixer
problem_formulation.objective_function: min_y Σ_i Σ_j σ_ij y_i y_j + Σ_i μ̂_i y_i subject to Σ_i y_i = D̂ and 0 ≤ y_i ≤ R_i, y_i ∈ Z
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Hard-constraint QAOA with custom XY and XYY ring mixers that preserve the sum constraint and feasible subspace; no penalty terms
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Phase-separation Hamiltonian C derived from the quadratic objective after quasi-binary substitution; mixer Hamiltonian B given in Eq. (12)

problem_instance.description: Portfolio optimization on NASDAQ stocks and a two-asset mixability test
problem_instance.dataset_name: NASDAQ historical returns; two-asset subset for mixability

dataset_specification.date_range: 2022-12-02 to 2023-02-28 for NASDAQ data; two-asset study uses NVDA and TSLA
dataset_specification.preprocessing: historical returns and covariance matrix computed from market prices; precision parameter α used to discretize weights

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Returns expectations and covariance matrix computed from historical closing prices; risk factor q set to 18.415 in one instance; target return μ set to 2‰; bounds and precision α varied across experiments
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Cumulative distribution of solution costs, approximation ratio, mixability metric M_p, repeated experiments (33 repeats for instance 1; 320 experiments per configuration for instance 2)

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Greedy feasible-solution construction for initial state; covariance/return estimation from historical prices; parameter scheduling methods (Sample20, OLS, IOLS, IQAOA)
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Brute-force computation of optimal and worst costs for approximation ratio; cumulative distribution and confidence intervals; repeated runs for error bars

speedup_claims.caveats: No asymptotic or empirical quantum speedup is claimed; the paper reports simulation-based performance only.

advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Would require a fault-tolerant or substantially larger-scale implementation; the paper only reports noiseless numerical simulations and no hardware advantage benchmark.
limiting_factors: No classical baseline that is a direct runtime competitor
COBYLA parameter search dominates the workflow
Problem sizes are small (18 qubits for main instance, 12 qubits for mixability study)

notes: Hardware inferred as simulator because the paper states numerical simulations using Qiskit and does not name a physical QPU.
num_qubits reported as 18 for instance 1, 12 for the two-asset mixability study, and 96 for the high-precision iterative example; all are gate-based logical qubit counts.
Circuit depth reported as p = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16 for the QAOA experiments.
No asymptotic quantum speedup is claimed; the paper is an algorithmic proposal with empirical simulation results only.
The paper reports improved approximation ratios and mixability within a QAOA simulation study, but does not demonstrate quantum advantage over classical methods.
Classical brute force is used only as a reference for approximation ratio, not as a runtime comparison.

experiments.description: Two-asset mixability study for NVDA and TSLA using quasi-binary encoding, with 12 qubits total and p = 1, 2, 4, 8 layers to evaluate mixability metric M_p.

algorithm.parameter_initialization: Discrete beta grid with beta_1 = ... = beta_p = i/4π, i = 1..7

key_results: Mixability improves with depth; at epsilon = 0.0001, the grayscale image becomes fully black by p = 8

experiments.description: Precision-increasing iterative method applied to QB-QAOA on the portfolio instance from Section 4.4.1, using p = 8, CVaR-QAOA, IQAOA scheduling, lambda = 0.5, and six iterations.

algorithm.variant: QB-QAOA with precision-increasing iterative method; CVaR-QAOA; IQAOA scheduling
algorithm.parameter_initialization: Iterative refinement from coarse to finer precision

key_results: All six iterations used 18 qubits in simulation
Solution quality improved monotonically across iterations
The worst solution in iteration 4 was already better than the best solution in iteration 1
